durations.use: Tooltip dismiss, press release. Barely reads as motion.
The default exit. Hover, focus ring, checkbox, switch track.
Dropdown, popover, context menu, backdrop, collapse.
Dialog, toast, switch thumb — a surface arriving.
Progress and meter fills. Data moving, not chrome.

easings.use: Anything arriving. Fast start, long settle. The house curve.
Anything repositioning while staying on screen.
Dialog, popover, switch. At most one per screen.
A sampled spring: one soft overshoot, then it settles. Something physical landing — a thumb, an arrow, a released sheet. Never on a data value.

amplitudes.use: Tooltip — stays glued to its anchor.

rules: **Duration and easing are class names, not numbers.** `duration-base`, `ease-entrance`. Tailwind has no `--duration-*` theme namespace, so WunderUI ships these as `@utility` rules that also set `--tw-duration` — which means they work on `animate-in` / `animate-out` too.
**Only `transform` and `opacity`.** Everything else goes through layout or paint. Height animates via `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr`, never via `height`.
**Entrances decelerate, exits accelerate.** `ease-entrance` in, `ease-exit` out — and the exit is one step shorter on the duration scale, never the entrance duration reversed.
**Never fade in the LCP element.** An element at `opacity: 0` is not an LCP candidate, so a 600ms hero fade adds 600ms to your LCP. Render headline copy at full opacity; animate `transform` only.
**Restrain the travel.** Anything anchored to a trigger moves `--travel-xs` or `--travel-sm`. A menu that slides 20px looks like it fell in.

**One overshoot per screen.** `ease-overshoot` is punctuation. Two of them on one view and the interface reads as a toy. Never on a data value: a bar, gauge or bubble that swings past its number shows a wrong number for a moment.

**Reduced motion is opt-in, not a kill switch.** Wrap the animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so the still state is the default and you cannot forget a selector. Reduced means calmer, not nothing: drop transforms and travel, keep opacity and colour changes (rule 15).

**Never `transition-all`.** Name the properties — `transition-[opacity,transform]` — or use bare `transition`, which covers colour, shadow, transform and opacity but no layout property. `transition-all` animates things you did not mean to animate, including on first paint.
**Loading keeps its height.** A skeleton occupies the same box as the content it stands in for, and crossfades — it never collapses and reflows.
**A looping ambient animation is the one place `ease-in-out` belongs.** A shimmer that runs forever has no entrance and no exit, so symmetry is correct there and nowhere else.

**Animate by frequency.** Keyboard-driven and 100+/day actions (command palette, shortcuts, moving between tooltips) get no motion; tens a day get a short fade; rare moments may delight. Tooltips skip their entrance when another one was just open (`data-open:data-instant:animate-none`).

**Anchored surfaces grow from their trigger.** Popover, dropdown, tooltip, hover card and select use `origin-(--transform-origin)`. Never start from `scale(0)` — start at 0.92–0.97 with opacity. Centred dialogs are exempt.

**Toggles stay interruptible.** Animate switches, checkboxes, tabs and other repeated state changes with transitions — they retarget from wherever they are — never with keyframes bound to the state, which restart from zero. An overshoot transition (`transition-transform duration-base ease-overshoot`) still swings past the end.

**Hover only where hover exists.** Tailwind v4's `hover:` is already gated to `(hover: hover)`; hand-written `:hover` in CSS goes inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, so a tap on a phone does not leave a hover state stuck.

**Reduced motion keeps the fade.** WunderUI's global rule zeroes the scale, slide, spin and blur of every `animate-in` / `animate-out` and every transform transition, and keeps opacity and colour — so do not add `motion-reduce:transition-none` or `motion-reduce:animate-none` to a fade.

/* Dialog, sheet, popover, dropdown, context menu — one pattern for all of them.
   Base UI exposes data-open / data-closed; tw-animate-css turns them into keyframes. */
<Dialog.Popup className="
  data-open:animate-in   data-open:fade-in-0   data-open:zoom-in-92
  data-open:slide-in-from-bottom-2
  data-open:duration-slow  data-open:ease-overshoot
  data-closed:animate-out  data-closed:fade-out-0 data-closed:zoom-out-96
  data-closed:duration-fast data-closed:ease-exit
" />

parts.name: Accordion
parts.description: Holds which items are open. Opening one item closes the open one unless you set `multiple`.

parts.name: AccordionItem
parts.description: One section, framed as a bordered `card` (the default) or as a `divider` row with a line above and below.

parts.name: AccordionTrigger

items.text: Use an Accordion for a list of sections people read one at a time, such as an FAQ or grouped settings. For a single show-more panel, use Collapsible; for views of one object, use Tabs.
Keep one `variant` per list: `card` items for a stand-alone list, `divider` items inside a surface that already has a frame.
Set `multiple` on `Accordion` when people compare answers. By default, opening one item closes the one that was open.
Write the trigger as the question or the section name in sentence case: `How do refunds work?`. It is the button's accessible name.
Don't put buttons or links inside `AccordionTrigger`. The whole row is already a `<button>`, and a control nested in it is not reliably reachable by keyboard.

parts.name: Avatar
parts.description: The round or square frame in five sizes from `sm` to `xl`. Set `color` for tinted initials or `variant="primary"` for a filled one.

parts.name: AvatarImage
parts.description: The photo. It shows once it has loaded; until then, or when the URL fails, the fallback stays in its place.

parts.name: AvatarFallback
parts.description: Initials or an icon, shown while the image loads or when there is none. The text size follows the avatar size.

parts.name: AvatarBadge
parts.description: A status dot at the bottom corner: inside the edge of a circle, on the corner of a square. Its icon hides on the two smallest sizes.

items.text: Use an Avatar to show who a person or workspace is, next to their name. For several people in little space, use Avatar Group or Avatar Stack.
Always add an `AvatarFallback` with initials, also when there is an image. It covers the moment before the photo loads and a broken image URL.
Give `AvatarImage` the person's name as `alt` when the avatar stands alone, and `alt=""` when the name is printed right beside it.
Use `color` for initials avatars and keep the same hue per person. The tints are theme tokens, so the initials stay readable in dark mode.
Don't resize an avatar with classes like `size-12`. Pick `size` (`sm`, `xs`, `default`, `lg`, `xl`): initials, icon and badge scale with it.

parts.name: AvatarGroupCount

items.text: Use an Avatar Group to show who is on a project or document, composing each avatar yourself. For people passed as data with a built-in limit, use Avatar Stack.
Cut the list yourself and put the rest in `AvatarGroupCount` as `+12`. The group renders every child it gets; it does not count or hide anyone.
Place the group on a surface that sets `--surface`, such as a Card. The rings take that colour, so each avatar reads as cut out of the background.
Don't mix avatar sizes in one group. The overlap and the size of the count circle assume one `size` for every avatar.

parts.name: BadgeCell
parts.description: A Badge for a table cell, made from a `label` string, with the `light_border` style by default.

items.text: Use a Badge for a short status or category on a row or card: `Paid`, `Draft`, `Beta`. For a change in a number, use Trend Chip; for a message people need to read, use Alert.
Give each status one `color` and keep it wherever that status appears. Write the status in the label too, so colour is never the only cue.
Use `light` or `light_border` in tables and lists and keep the solid `plain` style for the one badge that should stand out. `BadgeCell` already uses `light_border`.
Pass `render={<button />}` when the badge does something, such as removing a filter. Only a `<button>` or `<a>` gets the pointer, the hover ring and the focus ring.
Don't recolour a badge with classes or hex values. Every `color` and `badgeStyle` pair is measured for AA contrast in light and dark mode.

items.text: Use a Breadcrumb on nested pages, such as one project's settings, so people see where they are and can step back up. For switching between sibling views, use Tabs.
End the trail with `BreadcrumbPage`, not a link. It carries `aria-current="page"`, so screen readers announce where the person is.
Put a `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items yourself; the list does not add them. Each one sits in its own `<li>` and is hidden from assistive technology.
Don't link the current page or set `aria-current` on a link by hand. `BreadcrumbPage` already marks the last step and is not clickable.

items.text: Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, send, open a dialog. A move to another page is a link: pass `render={<a href=… />}` together with `nativeButton={false}`.
Give each view one `primary` button for its main action. Every other action is `plain` or a link.
Label it with a verb and its object: `Save changes`, `Invite member`. A destructive button repeats the action; the button next to it says `Cancel`.
Don't use `outline` for ordinary secondary actions. In WunderUI the secondary button is `plain`; `outline` is the indigo-rimmed accent for the rare case that needs one.
Don't set heights or paddings by hand (`h-9`, `px-6`). Pick a `size`: the sizes read the density tokens, so compact and comfortable both stay right.

Give every IconButton an `aria-label` that names the action: `Delete invoice`, not `Trash`. A tooltip is extra help, not the name.
Set `variant="plain"` or `ghost` for secondary icon actions. The default is `primary`, and a view has one primary action.
Pass `label` to IconButtonTextCell. Without it every row's button is announced as `Action`.
Don't use `sm` or `md` as the only control on a touch screen. Pick `xl` or `2xl`, which reach the 44 px hit area the polish rules ask for on touch.

items.text: Use a Button Group for a few related actions that belong together, such as zoom in and zoom out or previous and next. For one choice that stays selected, use a Radio Button Group.
Give the group an `aria-label` that names what the buttons do together, such as `Zoom`. It already has `role="group"`, but no name.
Use the same `variant` and `size` on every button inside. The shared borders only line up when the buttons have the same height and border.
Don't wrap the buttons in extra elements. Corners and overlaps are set on direct children only, so a wrapper breaks the joined edges.
Don't put a primary button into the group. A view has one primary action, and the joined edges present the buttons as equals.

items.text: Use a Card to group content about one thing, such as a project, a plan or a settings section. For a row with icon, title and meta, use Item Card; when there is nothing to show yet, use Empty State.
Leave the padding to the card: the default size has the same 20 px inset as the chart, stat and metric cards. Use `size="sm"` for dense grids instead of overriding `p-*` classes.
Put a menu or one small button in `CardAction`. It stays top right however long the title runs.
Use plain buttons in `CardFooter` when cards repeat in a grid. A view has one primary action, and a primary button on every card leaves none.
Don't set `bg-white` or a hex background on a card. `bg-card` follows the theme and dark mode, and the parts inside read it through `--surface`.

Keep the number of tabs small enough for a phone. The row scrolls sideways when it runs out of room, and a tab past the edge is easy to miss.

items.text: Use an Agenda for a short, read-only list of what happens when, such as a day's meetings. For past events in order, use Timeline; for rows with guests, a menu or a click action, use Agenda Event.
Sort `items` by time before passing them in. The list renders them in array order.
Write `time` in one short format across the list, such as `09:30`. The time column is narrow and fixed, so a long range wraps onto a second line.
Set `color` to a CSS variable such as `var(--primary)`, not a hex. The value goes straight into an inline style, and only a token follows the theme and dark mode.
Don't make the Agenda clickable by wrapping it in a link or button. Its rows have no hover or focus state; use Agenda Event with `onClick` when an entry opens something.

items.text: Use an Action Bar for bulk actions on rows someone has selected: export, archive, delete. For actions that are always available, use Toolbar.
Show the bar only while something is selected and put the count in `label`: `3 selected`. The count tells people what the buttons will act on.
Give icon-only buttons in the bar an `aria-label`. The bar has no role or name of its own, so each button has to carry its own name.
Place the bar yourself, for example fixed and centred near the bottom of the view. `ActionBar` draws the pill; it neither positions nor animates itself.
Don't run a destructive bulk action straight from the bar. Confirm it in an Alert Dialog that names how many items go: `Delete 3 invoices?`.

Set `label` to what the row holds: `Template previews`. It names the region, and the default `Carousel` tells nobody what is inside.
Drive dots or thumbnails through `index` and `onIndexChange` instead of scrolling the strip yourself. The carousel springs to the slide and reports the one in view.
Keep `autoPlay` for images, not text. It pauses on hover, focus, a hidden tab and reduced motion, but moving slides are hard to read.

Say what will appear and why it is empty, then offer one action: `No invoices yet`, `They appear here as soon as the first one is sent.` and `New invoice`.
For a search without results, name the query and offer a way out: `No results for “invoice 2024”` with `Clear search`.
Use the frameless `default` look inside a card that already has a border, and the `dashed` default where the empty state stands on the page.
Don't show a bare `No results` line. Without a reason and a next step, an empty place looks broken and leaves people stuck.

Use `onSelect` to react to the chosen file or folder (open it in a preview, show its details), and `selectedId` when the selection lives in your state; without it the tree keeps its own.

Keep `title` and `description` short or give the full text another way. Both are cut to one line with an ellipsis.
Use `meta` for a short fact with its unit, such as `2.4 MB` or `Updated 3 min ago`.

Set `compact` for long lists and milestones. Dots, text and gaps shrink so more entries fit.
Don't write times like `recently`. Give each `timestamp` a date or a time with its unit, such as `Oct 12, 14:30` or `3 min ago`.

Put widgets under a page heading of level two. The title renders as an `<h3>`, so the heading order stays intact.
Keep the header to one `action`, such as a plain `View all` button or an IconButton with an `aria-label`.

items.text: Use Autocomplete when the user may type anything and the list only suggests: a search box, a tag, a city. When the answer must be one of the items, use a Combobox.

Open on the right month with `defaultMonth`, or control it with `month` and `onMonthChange` when two calendars must move together.

Limit the choice with `min` and `max`, and block single days with `disabled` (a list of dates or a test such as weekends). Blocked days stay reachable with the arrow keys and are announced as unavailable; still say near the calendar why a day is blocked.

items.text: Use an Alert for a message that stays on the page until the cause is gone: a failed payment, a limit reached, a read-only workspace. For feedback on a finished action, use a toast.

Pick the `variant` by meaning: `negative` for what blocks the user, `warning` for what needs attention soon, `positive` for a confirmed state, `primary` for neutral news. `plain` is for notes without urgency.
Put the next step in the text or as one action button inside `Alert`: `Update payment method`. An alert that only states a problem leaves the user to find the fix.
Use `size="small"` for a one-line notice with a short title and description. Longer text belongs in `large`, where it wraps instead of truncating.
Don't pass `onClose` on an alert that reports a blocking problem. A dismissed error leaves the page looking healthy while the cause is still there.
Don't rely on the colour alone. The title or description has to say what is wrong, since the variants differ only by tint and icon.

Don't fire several toasts for one action. The stack shows four at most; older ones fade out.

items.text: Use PullToRefresh for a touch-first list or feed that the user reloads by hand. For data that updates itself, show the new state and skip the gesture.
Return the promise from `onRefresh`. The spinner and the lock stay until it settles, also when it fails, so a slow request never looks finished.
Keep `threshold` at or below `maxPull` (defaults 70 and 110). The pull moves at half the finger speed, so the user drags about twice the threshold.
Don't make the gesture the only way to refresh. It is pointer-based with no keyboard route, so give keyboard and screen reader users a visible `Refresh` button.
Don't expect a tap to work right after a pull. The click that ends a drag is swallowed on purpose, so the item under the finger is not opened.

Pass `asChild` when the child is already a button or a link. Without it you nest a `<button>` inside a `<button>`, which is invalid HTML.

Update `count` and `active` together in `onToggle`. The component keeps no state, so toggling without changing `active` leaves the pill unchanged.
Set `active` for the reactions the current user made, so the tint and `aria-pressed` show which ones they can take back.

Choose `side="bottom"` for phones and `right` for desktop detail views. The bottom sheet is capped at 80vh, the side sheets at `max-w-sm`.
